events.title: Octavian takes Alexandria and Mark Antony takes his own life
events.description: Octavian's army entered Alexandria and Mark Antony, defeated and deserted, killed himself. Cleopatra's suicide days later ended the Ptolemaic dynasty and Egypt became a Roman province.

events.title: Ibrahim II of Ifriqiya captures Taormina from the Byzantines
events.description: Aghlabid forces led by Ibrahim II of Ifriqiya took Taormina, the last great citadel in Byzantine hands in Sicily, after volunteers climbed its unwatched seaward face. Its fall concluded the Muslim conquest of Sicily.
events.html: Aghlabid forces led by Ibrahim II of Ifriqiya took Taormina, the last great citadel in Byzantine hands in Sicily, after volunteers climbed its unwatched seaward face. Its fall concluded the Muslim conquest of Sicily.

events.title: Swiss cantons swear the alliance celebrated as Switzerland's birth
events.description: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden concluded a perpetual defensive alliance, recorded in the Federal Charter dated early August 1291. 1 August is now Swiss National Day.
events.html: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden concluded a perpetual defensive alliance, recorded in the Federal Charter dated early August 1291. 1 August is now Swiss National Day.

events.title: Queen Anne dies, ending the Stuart line
events.description: Queen Anne died without surviving children, the last Stuart monarch. Under the Act of Settlement the crown passed to George, Elector of Hanover, beginning the Hanoverian dynasty.
events.html: Queen Anne died without surviving children, the last Stuart monarch. Under the Act of Settlement the crown passed to George, Elector of Hanover, beginning the Hanoverian dynasty.

events.title: Joseph Priestley isolates oxygen
events.description: By heating mercuric oxide, Joseph Priestley produced a gas in which a candle burned with remarkable vigour. He called it 'dephlogisticated air'; Lavoisier later named it oxygen.
events.html: By heating mercuric oxide, Joseph Priestley produced a gas in which a candle burned with remarkable vigour. He called it 'dephlogisticated air'; Lavoisier later named it oxygen.

events.title: France's Convention adopts the metric system
events.description: The National Convention decreed a provisional metre, based on a fraction of the Earth's meridian, as France's unit of length. The decimal metric system has since been adopted almost worldwide.
events.html: The National Convention decreed a provisional metre, based on a fraction of the Earth's meridian, as France's unit of length. The decimal metric system has since been adopted almost worldwide.

events.title: Germany declares war on Russia
events.description: After Russia refused to halt mobilisation, Germany declared war on it. The declaration turned the Austro-Serbian conflict into a general European war within days.
events.html: After Russia refused to halt mobilisation, Germany declared war on it. The declaration turned the Austro-Serbian conflict into a general European war within days.

events.title: The Warsaw Uprising begins
events.description: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupiers of Warsaw. After 63 days, with the Red Army halted across the Vistula, the uprising was crushed and the city systematically destroyed.
events.html: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupiers of Warsaw. After 63 days, with the Red Army halted across the Vistula, the uprising was crushed and the city systematically destroyed.
